# For this assignment, I'm creating an awful plot and a pretty good one using data on collegiate sports budgets

### The first step is always loading in our libraries!

```{r}
##### Load Libraries #####

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(scales)
```

### The second step is reading in our data

For this assignment, I chose the Collegiate Sports Budgets from Equity in Athletics Data Analysis. NPR wrote an article about this. Cool!

```{r}
##### Read in Data #####
sports <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2022/2022-03-29/sports.csv')

write_csv(sports, here("Goodplot-badplot", "Data", "sports.csv"))
```

### The third step is cleaning up the data

I wanted to highlight the budgets from the year 2019 since that is the most recent year in the data set. I also chose to focus on Men's Tennis because I play tennis!

```{r}
tennis_college <- sports |>
  filter(year == "2019", # Choosen year
         sports == "Tennis", # Tennis only
         classification_name == "NCAA Division I-FBS", # Select for Division
         exp_men > 1050000, # This is cut off for top 20 expenses
         !is.na(exp_men)) |> # Get rid of NA values in expenses
  mutate(exp_men = as.numeric(exp_men)) |> # Change to numeric
  arrange(desc(exp_men)) # Order from highest to lowest

```

As a part of cleaning up the data, I noticed that the exp_men column was not written as a dollar amount. I created a new column that adds the dollar sign and "," as the digital group separator to each exp_men value.

```{r}
tennis_college <- tennis_college |>
  mutate(exp_men_price = label_dollar(prefix = "$ ", big.mark = ",")(exp_men)) # Adding new column: 1000 would become $ 1,000
```

I also wanted to make the names of the colleges easier to read. I adjusted the names of the top 20 schools in Men's Tennis expenses to their more commonly used name.

```{r}
##### Adjust College Names #####

tennis_college$institution_name[tennis_college$institution_name == "Baylor University"] <- "Baylor"
tennis_college$institution_name[tennis_college$institution_name == "Texas Christian University"] <- "TCU"
tennis_college$institution_name[tennis_college$institution_name == "University of Louisville"] <- "Louisville"
tennis_college$institution_name[tennis_college$institution_name == "Texas A & M University-College Station"] <- "Texas A&M"
tennis_college$institution_name[tennis_college$institution_name == "Wake Forest University"] <- "Wake Forest"
tennis_college$institution_name[tennis_college$institution_name == "Ohio State University-Main Campus"] <- "Ohio State"
tennis_college$institution_name[tennis_college$institution_name == "University of Oklahoma-Norman Campus"] <- "Oklahoma"
tennis_college$institution_name[tennis_college$institution_name == "University of Florida"] <- "Florida"
tennis_college$institution_name[tennis_college$institution_name == "University of California-Los Angeles"] <- "UCLA"
tennis_college$institution_name[tennis_college$institution_name == "University of Southern California"] <- "USC"
tennis_college$institution_name[tennis_college$institution_name == "Southern Methodist University"] <- "SMU"
tennis_college$institution_name[tennis_college$institution_name == "The University of Texas at Austin"] <- "Texas"
tennis_college$institution_name[tennis_college$institution_name == "Auburn University"] <- "Auburn"
tennis_college$institution_name[tennis_college$institution_name == "Clemson University"] <- "Clemson"
tennis_college$institution_name[tennis_college$institution_name == "University of Michigan-Ann Arbor"] <- "Michigan"
tennis_college$institution_name[tennis_college$institution_name == "Louisiana State University and Agricultural & Mechanical College"] <- "LSU"
tennis_college$institution_name[tennis_college$institution_name == "Vanderbilt University"] <- "Vanderbilt"
tennis_college$institution_name[tennis_college$institution_name == "University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign"] <- "Illinois"
tennis_college$institution_name[tennis_college$institution_name == "University of Georgia"] <- "Georgia"
tennis_college$institution_name[tennis_college$institution_name == "University of Notre Dame"] <- "Notre Dame"
```

I didn't know if there was a shorter way to do this so had to go one by one!

### After I cleaned up all the data, I could make my bad plot.

```{r}
#| label: fig-bad-plot
#| fig-cap: "tenns Collage budget Sport 10 1-FCS"
#| fig-cap-location: bottom
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-align: "center"

bad_mten_budget <- ggplot(data = tennis_college,
                           mapping = aes(x = institution_name,
                                         y = exp_men)) +
  geom_col(width = 5, fill = "#4A412A", color = "#CFFF04", linewidth = 5) + # Ugly color choices
  geom_text(aes(label = exp_men_price), hjust = -0.2, size = 10, color = "#ff3503") + # Adding labels to each bar in the graph
  scale_y_reverse(
    breaks = seq(0, 2000000, by = 500000), # Flipping the graph upside down, reversing the y axis 
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .5)) # Creating space between top of graph and where bars start
  ) +
  labs(title = "Budgat College tenns sportt 10 1-FBS",
       x = "Dolla dolla bills yall", y = "Institution of higher education where people go to learn about stuff",
       caption = "Source: Equity in Athletics Data Analysis"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#00FF00", color = "black", linewidth = 10),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#4A412A"), # Adding background color here
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "#FF0000", linewidth = 4), # Changing major gridlines 
    panel.grid.minor = element_line(color = "#FFFF00", linewidth = 10), # Changing minor gridlines
    plot.title = element_text(size = 60, hjust = .5, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 15, hjust = .5),
    plot.caption = element_text(vjust = -2), 
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 24, face = "bold", vjust = -1.5),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 2),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 20, hjust = 1, face = "italic")
  )

bad_mten_budget

ggsave(here("Goodplot-badplot", "Outputs", "fig-bad-plot.png"), width = 11, height = 8)
```

#### Some of the bad plotting practices include:

- Is it clear?

  - The title does not clearly identify what the plot is displaying and there are spelling mistakes

  - The x and y axis titles are unclear, do not include units, and are not formatted the same. They are also on the wrong axes

- Does it communicate data responsibly?

  - The border of the graph cuts off the plot title and axis titles

  - The size of the title is way too large and the axis titles sizes and boldness are inconsistent

  - The X axis labels are too small

  - The graph is flipped upside down and there is a lot of empty space above \$0. Scaled incorrectly

- Does it look awesome?

  - The colors do not work well together, lots of neon and that brown is supposedly the ugliest color according to google

    - Not color blind friendly either

  - There is no context given what is shown in the graph

  - Major and minor grid lines are too large, not equal, different colors, and too many of them in general

  - Argument to be made that it looks awesome

  - Bars are overlapping, impossible differentiate which school they represent

### Now that the bad plot is done, we can try to make a good plot!

While the data is ready to be plotted, I wanted to enhance how the good plot would look by creating a color scale that attached each college to their primary color. That is done in the code below.

```{r}
##### Create Color Scale #####

college_colors <- scale_fill_manual(values = c(
  "Baylor" = "#154734",
  "TCU" = "#4D1979",
  "Louisville" = "#AD0000",
  "Texas A&M" = "#500000",
  "Wake Forest" = "#9E7E38",
  "Ohio State" = "#BA0C2F",
  "Oklahoma" = "#841617",
  "Florida" = "#0021A5",
  "UCLA" = "#2D68C4",
  "USC" = "#990000",
  "SMU" = "#354CA1",
  "Texas" = "#BF5700",
  "Auburn"= "#002B49",
  "Clemson" = "#F56600",
  "Michigan" = "#FFCB05",
  "LSU" = "#461D7C",
  "Vanderbilt" = "#CFAE70",
  "Illinois" = "#FF5F05",
  "Georgia" = "#BA0C2F",
  "Notre Dame" = "#0C2340"
))
```

### Now here is my good plot!

```{r}
#| label: fig-good-plot
#| fig-cap: "The Top 20 Expenses of Men's Tennis Teams for Division 1-FBS Schools"
#| fig-cap-location: bottom
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 9
#| fig-align: "center"

plot_mten_budget <- ggplot(data = tennis_college,
                            mapping = aes(x = exp_men,
                                          y = reorder(institution_name, exp_men),
                                          fill = institution_name)) +
  geom_col(width = .8) +
  college_colors + # This, with fill = institution_name sets the bar color to each colleges primary color 
  geom_text(aes(label = exp_men_price), hjust = -0.2, size = 4) + # Adding labels to end of bars to see what each value is specifically
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 2000000, by = 500000), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .3)), labels = label_number(prefix = "$", big.mark = ",")) + # Making sure the labels have the right formatting, changing x axis scale and creating more space on the right side of the graph
  labs(title = "The Top 20 Expenses of Men's Tennis Teams for Division 1-FBS Schools in 2019",
       x = "Men's Tennis Expenses ($)", y = "Institution Name",
       caption = "Source: Equity in Athletics Data Analysis"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 20, hjust = .5, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 15, hjust = .5),
    plot.caption = element_text(vjust = -1),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", vjust = -1.5),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, vjust = -1),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 1, margin = margin(r = 5)),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

plot_mten_budget

ggsave(here("Goodplot-badplot", "Outputs", "fig-good-plot.png"), width = 13, height = 9)
```

#### Some reasons why this is a good plot:

- Is it clear?

  - No grammatical errors, title accurately describes the plot, not too large

  - Axes include units when needed, clearly defined labels

  - In descending order so that the highest expense is at the top going down

  - Added bar labels to get the specific expenses value

- Does it communicate data responsibly?

  - Adequate use of space, no overlapping labels

  - Consistent size, boldness, fonts

  - Graph is horizontal to ensure y axis labels are readable and not overcrowded.

- Does it look awesome?

  - Colors of the bar represent the primary color of each college

  - Bars spaced properly, space in between to more easily differentiate between each school

### That is all. Thanks for viewing!
